notes_context:
Memory items from past tasks:
- [rb-0008] Compute strictly-after occurrences with floor division plus one: For periodic events from a start time, the first occurrence strictly after a timestamp is start + ((after - start) // length + 1) * length.
  Use integer floor division on timedeltas to find the index of the period containing `after`, then add one to get the strictly-next boundary. Handle the before-start case separately by returning start + length, since the start itself is not a renewal.
- [rb-0010] Check idempotency key before any state validation: When implementing money-moving operations, look up the idempotency key in the audit log first and return the original result before validating payment state or amounts.
  Team convention requires an optional keyword-only `idempotency_key=None` on every operation that changes a payment/credit/invoice balance. Scan `audit.events(<event_type>)` for a matching key and return the original record immediately; only then validate state. Include the key in the audit entry you write.
- [rb-0001] Use project money helpers for rounding: Monetary results must be rounded with the repository's own round_money helper, not Python's round() or bare Decimal.quantize().
  Before returning any Decimal money value, check ledgerly/money.py for a round_money (or similar) helper and wrap the final result with it. Python's round() and default quantize() use banker's rounding, which produces wrong invoice totals.
- [rb-0002] Read the money module before implementing money logic: Inspect ledgerly/money.py early to discover ZERO, to_money, and round_money conventions used across the codebase.
  Existing functions like line_total and invoice_total show the pattern: convert inputs with to_money, accumulate with ZERO as the sum start, and round the final result with round_money. Mirror that pattern for any new money-returning function.
- [rb-0003] Handle empty/zero-denominator cases explicitly: Guard against division by zero and return the project's ZERO constant for empty inputs.
  When computing an average over a collection, sum the denominator first and return ZERO (the money module's zero constant) if it is zero, rather than dividing and risking ZeroDivisionError or returning a plain int 0.
- [rb-0004] Reuse existing money helpers for validation: Validate monetary inputs by converting through the module's existing to_money/round_money helpers rather than ad-hoc checks.
  When a codebase has money utilities like to_money and round_money, use them to normalize and compare against ZERO instead of writing custom Decimal parsing. This keeps rounding and type coercion consistent with the rest of the module.

review_comments: [team convention] Every operation that moves money or changes a payment, credit or invoice balance must accept an optional keyword-only `idempotency_key=None` (callers without a key keep working). Check the key first, before validating state: if an audit entry with the same key already exists (ledgerly.audit.events()), return the original result (for functions that return a record, the same record) without applying the operation again. Include `idempotency_key` in the audit entry you write. Introduced after the double-refund incident INC-204.
[team convention] Write the amount in audit entries as float(amount): the ledger service's JSON importer rejects Decimal values.

item.title: Check idempotency key before state validation
item.description: When adding an operation that moves money, look up the idempotency key in audit events first and return the original result before validating state or applying changes.
item.content: Team convention (INC-204): every money-moving or balance-changing function must accept keyword-only `idempotency_key=None`. Scan `audit.events(<event_type>)` for a matching key first; if found, return the original record unchanged. Only then validate state and mutate. Include `idempotency_key` in the audit entry you write.

item.title: Cast Decimal amounts to float in audit entries
item.description: Audit entries must store amounts as float(amount) because the ledger service's JSON importer rejects Decimal values.
item.content: When calling `audit.record(...)`, pass `amount=float(payment.amount)` rather than the raw Decimal. This is a repo-wide convention; violating it breaks downstream JSON import even if local tests pass.

item.title: Inspect sibling modules for conventions before implementing
item.description: Before writing a new function, read adjacent modules (audit, clock, errors, other payment/invoice ops) to discover implicit conventions like idempotency and serialization rules.
item.content: The first attempt failed because it only read the target file and tests, missing the idempotency and float conventions. Grep for `idempotency_key` and `audit.record` across the repo to surface team-wide patterns before coding.
